# v0.8.0b3 — Plug & Charge ends a manual pause

Beta of the integration and app. **0.6.1 remains stable.**

Changes compared with 0.8.0b2:

- **Plug in and charge:** when Virtual Plug & Charge grants a permitted car, a
  manual pause from before the connection ends. Reached targets, a wallbox lock,
  a switched-off charging release and newer queued commands still keep charging
  stopped.
- **Departure plans first:** with an armed departure plan (manual or from the
  car), the release waits until the plan has paused until its calculated start
  or set its current, so charging never starts briefly before a planned pause.
- **No waiting after plug-in:** app 0.8.0b3 ends the pause while the charging
  release is still off. A current change without a possible charge no longer
  starts the state-change interval, so the release follows immediately.
- **The car's charge limit first:** each recognized connection starts with the
  car's own limit as the percentage target. A target at the car's limit follows
  every later change made in the car; a raised limit never resumes charging by
  itself.
- **Release only on request:** the new configuration switch **Switch off
  charging release when unplugged** closes the release after each disconnect when
  Virtual Plug & Charge is not used, so not every car can simply charge.
- **Why is charging blocked?** The Plug & Charge status sensor's
  **Blocking reason** attribute names the condition. Diagnostics also include
  the pause, release and goal-stop intents and the gate state, without session
  tokens.

Keep your existing HA entry and app data. When updating both components, update
the app to **0.8.0b3 through #apps-beta first**, wait for initialization, then
update the integration. With an older app, the release after ending a pause can
wait for the state-change interval. Ordinary service connections still require
**API 2 and service 0.6.1 or newer**; Plug & Charge needs **app 0.8.0b1 or
newer**. **#apps stays on stable 0.6.1.** Direct USB/LAN needs no app.
